authority: Ruled by the assistant at the operator's explicit delegation, under the determination doctrine of 2026-08-04 rev. 2. Recorded as the assistant's ruling, not the operator's.
reason: The doctrine as first issued ruled KEYLESS where no prior named the subject, including entries whose citations support nothing. That contradicts patch_kk21n, shipped hours earlier by the same author, which prints at the operator: 'A KEYLESS ruling here asserts the entry went beyond priors that ground nothing - KEYED by rule is the defensible read (4.03).' Same fact, opposite conclusions. The patch is right on the doctrine's own stated principle: keyless is the faculty-bearing number and a contested reading resolves toward the smaller one. Effect: keyless 112 -> 86, and its citation-defect rate falls because the corrected entries are precisely the defective population.

KKR-20260804-08.why: CORRECTED from keyless. cite_integrity finds this entry UNSUPPORTED: none of its 2 cited item(s) shares discriminating vocabulary with the claim. A KEYLESS ruling asserts the entry went beyond its declared priors; where the priors ground nothing, there is no readable prior to have gone beyond and the assertion is unsupportable. The forecaster may have held the right item in view and cited badly - the record cannot say. 4.03 defaults KEYED where the determination cannot be made, and the determination doctrine's own rule requires taking the reading that does not inflate the faculty-bearing count. Keyed by rule, not by judgment.
